title: Palindromic Substrings
statement: You get a string. Count how many of its substrings (runs of consecutive letters) read the same forwards and backwards. Substrings at different positions count separately, even if their letters are equal.

example.caption: aaa has 6: three single a, two aa (positions 0-1 and 1-2) and one aaa.

output.label: answer = 6 (the whole string aaa is one of them)

idea.sentence: Every palindrome mirrors around a centre, so from each letter and each gap between letters grow outward, and every time the two ends match, that window is one more palindrome to count.

jargon.plain: Text that reads the same left to right and right to left.
A run of consecutive letters. Two runs at different positions are different substrings.
The middle of a palindrome. A letter if its length is odd, the gap between two letters if it is even.

rows.name: Brute force
rows.note: n² substrings, each checked in up to n steps.

rows.name: Expand around centres
rows.note: 2n - 1 centres, each can grow up to n / 2 steps. Counting is one addition per match.

rows.name: DP table (n × n)
rows.note: isPal[i][j] is true when s[i] = s[j] and the inside is a palindrome. Same time, more memory.

fast.takeaway: Each matching window is exactly one palindrome, so counting needs no table, just a running total while growing.

stages.title: Count starts at 0
stages.note: One counter for every palindrome found.

stages.title: Grow and count
stages.note: While the letters at l and r match, s[l..r] is a palindrome: add one, then widen the window.

stages.title: Centre finished
stages.note: The growth stopped on a mismatch or an edge. Move to the next centre.

stages.title: Answer
stages.note: The counter holds the total over all odd and even centres.

edges.title: Single letter
edges.why: One letter is a palindrome of length 1. The odd centre counts it and the even centre finds nothing.

edges.title: Equal letters are separate
edges.why: Two single a at different positions, plus the pair aa. Equal text at different places counts again.

edges.title: All the same letter
edges.why: Every substring is a palindrome, so the answer is n(n + 1) / 2. This is the slowest input: each centre grows the longest.

edges.title: No repeats
edges.why: Only the single letters are palindromes. Every even centre fails on its first test.

gotchas.text: Count a window each time the ends match, before widening. A palindrome that grows five times gives five counts, not one.
Odd and even centres are both needed. Skipping even centres misses every palindrome like abba.
Check l >= 0 and r < s.length before reading s[l] and s[r]. s[-1] is undefined rather than an error, so a missing check can quietly count wrong.
s[i] is a byte. This works for ASCII letters. For text with accents or emoji, convert to []rune first, or the counts will be off.

recap.key: From each of the 2n - 1 centres grow outward while the ends match. Every matching window is one palindrome, so add one each time.
moves: For each index c, try an odd centre (c, c) and an even centre (c, c + 1)
While l >= 0, r < n and s[l] == s[r]: count one, then l-- and r++
Move on when the ends differ or an edge is hit
